title: Time-ordered free energy in correlated quantum systems: An agentic approach
authors: Ruo Cheng Huang, Isha Singh Le Xue, Yuxuan Qu, Paul M. Riechers, Varun Narasimhachar, Mile Gu
abstract: How much work can an agent extract from a temporal sequence of quantum states when it can only operate online under causal constraints---deciding which energy extraction method to use with knowledge of what it has observed before? Here, we study this problem in the context of quantum state sequences that are potentially non-Markovian---generated by some underlying hidden Markov machine that the agent cannot observe. Using techniques from dynamic programming and computational mechanics, we present a method to identify the provably optimal agent strategy, with time complexity that scales linearly with sequence length. This motivates us to introduce the maximum work such agents can extract---time-ordered free energy(TOFE)---as a fundamental measure of free energy available in a temporally correlated quantum system subject to causal considerations.
summary: This paper introduces Time-Ordered Free Energy (TOFE) as the fundamental measure of available free energy when extracting work from correlated quantum states under causal limitations. It develops an optimal strategy using dynamic programming that scales linearly with sequence length, providing a powerful tool for analyzing non-Markovian quantum processes.
main_problem: The core problem is determining the maximum work an agent can extract from a sequence of quantum states generated by a hidden, non-Markovian process while adhering to strict causal constraints.
main_result: They introduce Time-Ordered Free Energy (TOFE) as the fundamental measure for available free energy in such systems and develop an optimal strategy solvable via dynamic programming in linear time complexity.
method: The methodology employs a resource-theoretic framework, using dynamic programming over belief states derived from Bayesian inference to find the optimal causal policy.
model_or_system: The system models quantum state sequences generated by a Hidden Markov Model (HMM), where an agent interacts online with the emitted quantum system.
key_observables: Time-Ordered Free Energy (TOFE), Causal Dissipation ($\delta$), and various work extraction rates ($	ext{f}_{	ext{TO}}$, $	ext{w}_{	ext{LO}}$).
important_parameters: Sequence length $L$, temperature parameter $ eta$, and the belief state uncertainty quantified by entropy.
main_assumptions: The agent operates under strict causality (actions depend only on past observations), and the DP approach assumes belief states are sufficient statistics for optimization.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the perturbed coin process source, causal networks showing agent-system interaction, and comparisons of work deficit versus calculated causal dissipation across different sequence lengths.
paper_structure: The paper builds from defining the physical problem (causal work extraction) to developing the computational solution (DP in $O(L)$), establishing key theoretical relationships like Causal Dissipation ($\delta$), and finally addressing implementation details via spectral tagging for unitary updates.
why_interesting: This work provides a rigorous, information-theoretic framework for quantifying irreversibility and extractable energy in open quantum systems subject to realistic measurement constraints, which is highly relevant to non-equilibrium thermodynamics in AMO physics.
